target.title: Preview session workspace images and unsupported files
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Current `main` already owns session workspace text viewing and editing. The remaining gap is binary preview behavior: browser-safe images need a bounded inline preview, while unsupported binary files need a clear metadata-only state instead of lossy UTF-8 replacement text.

AI-assisted: yes, implemented and verified with Codex.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Keeps the existing session workspace file owner boundary and adds only optional preview metadata.
- Strictly decodes text, sniffs file content server-side, and base64-encodes only AVIF, GIF, JPEG, PNG, and WebP.
- Preserves the existing 256 KiB read cap and fs-safe path, symlink, and hardlink guards.
- Renders unsupported binaries as metadata without issuing an editable content hash.
- Preserves the current-main OpenClawKit API: `AgentsWorkspaceFile.encoding` remains `AnyCodable`, with a compile-time compatibility test.
- Renders hostile or unusual unsupported filenames literally instead of interpreting them as Markdown.

## User Impact

Users can preview supported session workspace images inline. Unsupported binary files show their path, MIME type, size, and update time without corrupt text. Existing text editing behavior and existing Swift callers remain source-compatible.

## Evidence

Exact proof head: `b22197d3fef2901e501baa12cce223bb840c6fb2`  
Latest-main base used for the proof: `bbf79b19346a031000ff6ac2d5b473008357401b`

### Exact-head browser proof

The recorded flow clicks through text, a supported 5,920-byte PNG (below the 256 KiB cap), and an unsupported BMP fallback.

![Exact-head session workspace click-through](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/pr-proof-assets/main/openclaw/pr-95956/b22197d3fe/session-workspace-clickthrough.gif)

![Supported 5,920-byte PNG preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/pr-proof-assets/main/openclaw/pr-95956/b22197d3fe/05-png-preview.png)

![Unsupported BMP metadata fallback](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Solvely-Colin/pr-proof-assets/main/openclaw/pr-95956/b22197d3fe/06-bmp-fallback.png)

Artifact manifest and WebM: [exact-head proof packet](https://github.com/Solvely-Colin/pr-proof-assets/tree/main/openclaw/pr-95956/b22197d3fe)

### Commands and runs

- `run_8870a5318dfa` on exact head `b22197d3fe`: 68 gateway tests + 24 Control UI tests passed; `pnpm protocol:check`, `pnpm tsgo:ui`, and focused E2E lint passed; 2 Chromium E2Es passed with required WebM, PNG-preview, and BMP-fallback artifacts.
- `run_ac40b2a8e8a9` on the same patch before two unrelated main commits also passed core/core-test/UI type checks.
- Fresh branch autoreview returned no accepted/actionable findings after the filename-literalization fix. The final assertion-only E2E adjustment also passed focused autoreview.

target.title: fix: pre-update config snapshot blocked after transient read errors
target.body:
Closes #105431

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running an OpenClaw update would permanently lose the pre-update config backup for that process when the first snapshot attempt hit a transient read/write failure (disk pressure, file lock, etc.). Later update writes then skipped snapshotting even though no `.pre-update` file existed.

## Why This Change Was Made

`createPreUpdateConfigSnapshot` marked a config path as snapshotted before the best-effort read/write completed. That permanently blocked retries after transient IO errors. The tracker now records success only after the snapshot write completes, while still keeping the once-per-process skip after a successful snapshot.

## User Impact

Update flows can recover a pre-update config backup after a transient snapshot failure instead of silently proceeding without one for the rest of the process.

## Evidence

- Focused local tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/config.backup-rotation.test.ts` → 9 passed (includes new `retries after a transient read failure` case)
- Crabbox/Testbox warmup unavailable in this environment (`crabbox` binary sanity check failed); CI will cover remote proof
- Autoreview helper could not run (`codex` executable not installed); change is a 2-file tracker ordering fix with sibling test coverage

target.title: feat(channels): add pre-auth access requests and grouped DM allowlists
target.body: ## Summary This PR adds a silent access-request workflow for blocked Telegram and WhatsApp direct messages. - Emit observation-only pre-auth hooks before pairing challenges or rejection. - Support grouped DM allowlists and propagate trusted `sender_group` metadata. - Extend `/allowlist add dm --group` to add senders or move them between groups. - Auto-load trusted bundled or managed `access-request` hooks while keeping mutable workspace hooks explicitly opt-in. - Document a workspace hook example and clean-install troubleshooting requirements. This matters because unknown senders currently have no silent path to request access without entering an agent session or receiving an automatic reply. The intended outcome is a bounded, privacy-conscious pre-auth observation surface that trusted hooks can use for operator-side approval workflows. Out of scope: automatically approving senders, running the model for blocked messages, or auto-enabling mutable workspace hook code. Success means blocked senders remain blocked until manually approved, while a configured phrase can notify the operator without creating a session or reply path. Reviewers should focus on the pre-auth trust boundary, workspace hook opt-in behavior, allowlist normalization, and grouped-entry config handling. ## Linked context Which issue does this close? N/A - no linked issue. Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related? N/A. Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No known maintainer or owner request. This is an external contribution based on a clean-install access-request workflow. ## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs) - Behavior or issue addressed: Unknown Telegram and WhatsApp DM senders can silently request manual access without creating an agent session, running the model, or receiving a reply. - Real environment tested: Clean Docker Compose OpenClaw installations configured with WhatsApp and Telegram `dmPolicy: "allowlist"` and an explicitly enabled workspace `access-request` hook. - Exact steps or command run after this patch: 1. Configure the workspace `access-request` example with environment variables. 2. Run `openclaw config set tools.profile messaging`. 3. Run `openclaw config set commands.config true`. 4. Recreate the container with `docker compose down && docker compose up -d`. 5. Send the configured access phrase from a blocked WhatsApp number. 6. Approve the sender from the operator chat with `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp --group restricted `. - Evidence after fix: 1. WhatsApp blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 2. Operator receives the silent WhatsApp access request notification. 3. WhatsApp sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel whatsapp`. 4. WhatsApp admitted sender receives a normal agent response. 5. Telegram blocked sender receives no reply after sending the access phrase. 6. Operator receives the silent Telegram access request notification. 7. Telegram sender admitted via `/allowlist add dm --channel telegram`. - Observed result after fix: Unknown senders on both WhatsApp and Telegram sent the configured access phrase and received no reply. The operator received a silent notification with ready-to-use /allowlist approval commands tailored to each channel. After approval, the sender was admitted to the restricted group. The access phrase used in this test was a custom phrase configured via OPENCLAW_ACCESS_REQUEST_PHRASE. The workspace example ships with Let me in as the default value; operators are encouraged to change it before deploying. - What was not tested: Multi-account deployments were not tested live. - Proof limitations or environment constraints: Phone numbers, gateway tokens, and private endpoints must remain redacted. - Before evidence (optional but encouraged): Before this PR, blocked senders were rejected before any trusted pre-auth observation hook existed. ## Tests and validation Commands run: ```bash node scripts/check-docs-mdx.mjs docs README.md node --import tsx scripts/generate-bundled-channel-config-metadata.ts --check pnpm build git diff --check ``` Focused Vitest validation covered 18 files and 383 tests across Telegram, WhatsApp, hook loading, hook mapping, config reload, inbound metadata, and grouped allowlist edits. Focused Vitest command: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run extensions/telegram/src/channel.allowlist.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/dm-access.test.ts extensions/telegram/src/inbound-context.contract.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-accessors.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/config-schema.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/inbound/access-control.test.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply/monitor/process-message.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/commands-allowlist.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-meta.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/allowlist-config-edit.test.ts src/hooks/internal-hooks.test.ts src/hooks/loader.test.ts src/hooks/message-hook-mappers.test.ts src/plugins/wired-hooks-message.test.ts src/gateway/config-reload.test.ts src/gateway/server-reload-handlers.test.ts src/infra/heartbeat-runner.returns-default-unset.test.ts ``` WhatsApp E2E validation: ```bash node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts extensions/whatsapp/src/auto-reply.web-auto-reply.connection-and-logging.e2e.test.ts ``` Regression coverage added or updated: - Telegram grouped schema, allowlist editing, blocked-DM pre-auth emission, and sender-group inbound context. - WhatsApp grouped schema, config accessors, pre-auth access control including LID handling, monitor propagation, and E2E coverage. - Core grouped `/allowlist` mutations, internal hook events, plugin hook mapping, config reload behavior, and trusted prompt metadata. Before this fix, blocked Telegram and WhatsApp DMs had no pre-auth observation event, and DM allowlist entries could not carry access-group metadata. ## Risk checklist Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. The config schema adds optional grouped DM `allowFrom` entries. Existing string entries remain supported. No migration is required. Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`) Yes. What is the highest-risk area? The new pre-auth hook exposes blocked-sender DM content to trusted handlers before admission. How is that risk mitigated? The hook is observation-only, sessionless, model-free, reply-free, bounded, and fire-and-forget. Mutable workspace hooks remain explicitly opt-in. Trusted bundled or managed hooks may auto-load only when an account uses `dmPolicy: "allowlist"`. Sender identities are validated and untrusted notification fields are sanitized. ## Current review state What is the next action? Submit for maintainer review. What is still waiting on author, maintainer, CI, or external proof? CI and maintainer review pending. Which bot or reviewer comments were addressed? Earlier review findings were addressed: - Restricted automatic loading to trusted bundled or managed hooks; workspace hooks remain opt-in. - Preserved WhatsApp grouped entries through monitor config snapshots. - Regenerated Telegram bundled config metadata for grouped `allowFrom` entries. ## Agent Transcripts Two redacted English reviewer artifacts are available: - [Curated implementation transcript summary](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520597/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.en.md) — recommended for a quick review. - [Full translated implementation transcript](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/28520607/openclaw-pre-auth-agent-transcript.full.en.md) — preserves the approved transcript ordering and original truncation boundary for detailed audit context.

target.title: feat(memory): add multi-slot memory role architecture
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes a memory-plugin architecture flaw: OpenClaw currently has one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner even though the product, docs, bundled plugins, and runtime behavior already treat “memory” as several different responsibilities.

Today, factual recall, auto-capture, compaction, dreaming/consolidation, and user/session modeling are all forced through the same global selector. That makes documented memory stacks impossible or brittle: selecting one memory provider can unintentionally displace another provider that owns a different responsibility.

This PR corrects that mismatch by introducing purpose-specific memory role slots:

- `memory.recall`
- `memory.capture`
- `memory.compaction`
- `memory.dreaming`
- `memory.userModel`

The new role slots are the mechanism. The fix is that OpenClaw can now represent the memory architecture it already documents and partially implements.

## What Problem This Solves

This is a flaw fix, not just a feature request.

OpenClaw’s memory ecosystem is already multi-role:

- `memory-core` / QMD provide local factual recall/search over project memory, session transcripts, and Markdown/QMD corpora.
- Honcho provides cross-session user, agent, and session modeling.
- LanceDB provides embedding-backed long-term recall and auto-capture.
- Active Memory orchestrates recall before generation by using whichever provider owns recall.
- Memory Wiki compiles durable memory into a companion knowledge vault rather than replacing active memory.
- Dreaming/consolidation is a separate runtime responsibility from ordinary recall.

The current `plugins.slots.memory` contract cannot express that architecture. It treats every `kind: "memory"` provider as competing for one owner slot, even when the providers are designed to do different jobs. That leads to three concrete problems:

1. **Documented combinations are not representable.** Configs such as builtin/QMD recall + Honcho user modeling, LanceDB capture + local recall, or Active Memory over a selected recall provider cannot be modeled cleanly through one memory owner.
2. **Runtime behavior depends on exceptions and side paths.** Plugins that should compose have to rely on context-engine ownership, sidecar behavior, fallback logic, or plugin-specific handling instead of a shared contract.
3. **Diagnostics and lifecycle handling become misleading.** Startup, validation, status, doctor repair, skill publishing, uninstall cleanup, runtime memory resolution, and SDK-facing aliases need to know which provider owns which memory responsibility.

So while this PR adds new public config keys, the intent is corrective: make the config/runtime contract match the memory system OpenClaw already exposes.

## User Impact / Intended Outcome

After this PR, OpenClaw can express memory stacks that were previously documented or implied but not cleanly configurable:

- `memory-core` or QMD can own factual recall while Honcho owns user/session modeling.
- LanceDB can own recall and/or capture without forcing unrelated memory roles through the same selector.
- Active Memory can use the configured `memory.recall` provider instead of depending on hard-coded assumptions.
- Dreaming/consolidation can be selected separately from ordinary recall where supported.
- Memory Wiki can remain a companion compiled-knowledge layer beside active memory providers.
- Existing configs using `plugins.slots.memory` continue to work as recall selection.
- `openclaw doctor --fix` can migrate/canonicalize non-conflicting legacy memory-slot config while preserving the legacy key for plugin compatibility.

## Linked Context

Closes #60572.

Directly related memory-composition requests and prior proposals:

- #38874: supplementary/additive memory plugins alongside the primary memory slot.
- #2306: earlier closed PR proposing stackable memory plugins.
- #2080: earlier request for multiple simultaneous memory plugins and emerging memory architectures.
- #77714: pluggable persistent memory backend demand.

Dreaming and memory-role separation context:

- #85473: future protocol work for making dreaming implementable by non-`memory-core` memory plugins. This PR adds the `memory.dreaming` slot contract but does not implement that full protocol.
- #63067 and #65411: prior work around keeping dreaming behavior available when another plugin owns the legacy memory slot.
- #62275: previous selected-slot dreaming config behavior.

Runtime/diagnostic slot handling context:

- #76567 and #76495: configured memory-slot runtime checks should load/consult the selected memory plugin.
- #78540: doctor/status memory diagnostics could misreport configured memory providers.
- #76550: stale `plugins.slots.*` references could leave config unrecoverable until doctor cleanup was broadened.

Context-engine compatibility context:

- #77063, #77185, #76576, and #81843: context-engine registration and LosslessClaw-adjacent failures shaped the compatibility review for preserving the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` behavior while rejecting unsupported per-agent `contextEngine` config.

Future API/RFC context:

- #70823: future machine-readable slot ownership/provenance. This PR intentionally keeps scalar plugin IDs and solves the memory role composition layer first.

Memory-plugin interop research: the [supporting research document](https://github.com/kklouzal/rfcs/blob/rfc/multi-slot-memory-role-architecture/rfcs/0009/memory-plugin-interop-research.md) validates this PR as necessary architecture work, not optional extensibility: OpenClaw's own documentation already describes memory as a composable ecosystem where builtin/QMD recall, Honcho user/session modeling, LanceDB recall/capture, Active Memory orchestration, dreaming/consolidation, and Memory Wiki compilation can coexist, but current `origin/main` collapses every `kind: "memory"` provider into one exclusive `plugins.slots.memory` owner, making those documented combinations impossible or dependent on brittle exceptions. PR #88504 closes that product/docs/runtime gap by replacing the single memory owner with explicit role slots — `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel` — while preserving legacy `memory` as a recall shorthand, so the documented memory-plugin interop story becomes actually representable in config and runtime behavior.

## What Changes

- Adds canonical memory role slots: `memory.recall`, `memory.capture`, `memory.compaction`, `memory.dreaming`, and `memory.userModel`.
- Keeps legacy `plugins.slots.memory` as a backward-compatible shorthand for `memory.recall` during an extended migration window.
- Adds per-agent memory role-slot overrides under `agents.list[*].plugins.slots`, limited to memory roles plus legacy `memory`.
- Wires role-slot selection through config schema/types/help/docs, plugin activation, gateway startup preloading, runtime memory resolution, skill publishing, validation, doctor repair/preview, uninstall cleanup, status diagnostics, and SDK-facing aliases.
- Preserves the existing global `plugins.slots.contextEngine` path for LosslessClaw and other context-engine plugins.
- Explicitly rejects unsupported per-agent `agents.list[*].plugins.slots.contextEngine` overrides because agent-scoped context-engine semantics are outside this PR.

## Implementation Notes

- Adds `src/plugins/slot-resolution.ts` as the shared role-slot helper layer for canonical memory role keys, defaults, normalization, effective per-agent resolution, and configured selection collection.
- Updates config schema/types/help/labels/docs for global and per-agent memory role slots.
- Keeps `PluginSlotsConfig.contextEngine` for global plugin slots, and adds an agent-slot type/schema that omits `contextEngine`.
- Updates doctor legacy memory-slot handling so `doctor --fix` canonicalizes to `memory.recall` while retaining legacy `memory` during the compatibility window.
- Updates plugin loader/activation/startup resolution so explicit role-slot selections activate memory plugins without confusing default `memory-core` fallback with a user-selected plugin under restrictive allowlists.
- Extends validation to report missing role-slot plugin refs and validate schemas for plugins selected only by non-recall or per-agent memory roles.
- Extends skill publishing, status scanning, uninstall cleanup, memory runtime, dreaming, compaction provider, and SDK alias behavior to use the role-aware model.
- Keeps memory runtime registrations addressable by plugin id, so runtime recall dispatch follows the resolved global or per-agent `memory.recall` owner.
- Passes the session agent id into Pi embedded extension factory construction so safeguard compaction provider selection honors per-agent `memory.compaction` overrides in both normal session runs and manual/queued compaction paths.
- Updates bundled memory plugin manifests/docs to describe role support and the recall shorthand migration.

## Tests / Verification

Current PR branch:

- Branch: `kklouzal:feat/multi-slot-memory-architecture`
- Base target: `openclaw/openclaw:main`
- Latest pushed commit: `9040ece51de5aae8178225cf5d6e8f82dde1886d`

target.title: fix(realtime): add timeout to WebRTC offer requests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users starting a realtime WebRTC voice session could remain stuck waiting when the SDP offer request returned headers but the answer body stalled.

## Why This Change Was Made

The WebRTC offer fetch now uses an explicit 30s AbortController deadline that stays active until the SDP answer body has been read. The change keeps the existing setup cancellation and failure flow intact and limits the timeout to the WebRTC offer exchange.

## User Impact

Realtime voice setup now fails through the existing error state instead of spinning indefinitely when the offer response body stops progressing.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-webrtc.test.ts` passed: 19 tests.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- `.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local --engine claude` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Focused local fallback was used because the Blacksmith Testbox wrapper was unavailable in this environment.
- Exact-head browser proof at `8baa2577891bfa2d014c9c2f21d17e399e2269c1`: ran Chromium through a Vite-served Control UI module harness, `attachChatRealtimeActions(...).toggleRealtimeTalk()`, a stubbed browser `RTCPeerConnection`, and a same-origin local SDP offer endpoint that sent response headers and intentionally left the response body open. This is not live OpenAI proof, but it exercises the browser fetch/body-read/AbortSignal path and the `chat-realtime` state machine that drives the visible UI status.

Command:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'JS'
# starts Vite + same-origin /realtime/calls stalled response middleware
# launches Playwright Chromium
# imports /src/pages/chat/chat-realtime.ts in the browser
# calls attachChatRealtimeActions(state); await state.toggleRealtimeTalk()
JS
```

Redacted transcript:

```json
{
  "exactHead": "8baa2577891b63458448c88a2275a355909904f0",
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:<redacted>/",
  "browserResult": {
    "elapsedMs": 30150,
    "finalStatus": "error",
    "finalDetail": "The user aborted a request.",
    "active": false,
    "updates": [
      { "status": "connecting", "detail": null, "active": true },
      { "status": "idle", "detail": null, "active": false },
      { "status": "error", "detail": "The user aborted a request.", "active": false }
    ],
    "requests": [
      { "method": "talk.client.create", "params": { "sessionKey": "main" } }
    ],
    "peer": {
      "localDescription": { "type": "offer", "sdp": "offer-sdp" },
      "remoteDescription": null,
      "connectionState": "closed"
    },
    "stoppedTracks": ["track"]
  },
  "serverEvents": [
    {
      "phase": "request-start",
      "method": "POST",
      "url": "/",
      "authorization": "<redacted>",
      "contentType": "application/sdp",
      "xProof": "browser-same-origin-loopback"
    },
    { "phase": "data", "bytes": 9 },
    { "phase": "request-end", "bytes": 9 },
    {
      "phase": "response-headers-sent",
      "note": "same-origin body intentionally left open"
    },
    { "phase": "request-close", "bytes": 9 }
  ]
}
```

Observations:

- The browser sent the SDP `POST` with the expected authorization/content-type headers and 9-byte offer body.
- The same-origin server sent response headers but kept the answer body open, reproducing the stalled answer-body case without CORS/private-network interference.
- The Control UI realtime state machine left connecting state after ~30s, closed the peer without setting a remote description, stopped the media track, and ended in `realtimeTalkStatus="error"` with `realtimeTalkActive=false`.
- Chromium surfaces this abort as `The user aborted a request.` rather than the custom timeout message; the fake-timer unit test still verifies the custom abort reason on the lower-level transport path.
- Not run: live OpenAI Realtime API / real microphone permission prompt / screenshot or video artifact.

AI-assisted change.

target.body: What Problem This Solves Issue #104412 reports that recurring cron jobs with payload.kind="command" are silently skipped across gateway stop/start windows. While investigating the issue, I noticed the restart catch-up test suite only covered systemEvent jobs, leaving both command job recovery paths untested. Why This Change Was Made Without test coverage for command jobs in startup catch-up, there was no way to confirm the two recovery scenarios worked correctly: A job added but never run (no lastRunAtMs) whose nextRunAtMs falls inside a stop window A job whose nextRunAtMs was already advanced past a missed slot, requiring the allowCronMissedRunByLastRun fallback path Both scenarios needed coverage regardless of whether a production bug exists on current main. User Impact No behavior change. Tests only. Proves the restart catch-up machinery correctly handles recurring command jobs in both recovery paths on current main, closing the gap identified during investigation. Evidence Both new tests pass on current main (17/17 total in the suite):

target.title: fix(macos): fit onboarding window on short screens
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #98674.

The macOS onboarding window used a fixed preferred content height and `window.center()`, so on short visible desktop areas the first-run window could extend below the screen and hide the bottom setup/navigation action.

## Why This Change Was Made

This routes onboarding window placement through the existing `WindowPlacement.centeredFrame` helper so the actual NSWindow frame is clamped to the active screen visible frame before display. The SwiftUI root view now allows its height to shrink between the onboarding minimum and preferred height, so the clamped window can adapt instead of insisting on the full preferred height.

## User Impact

Users on shorter displays or desktops with reduced visible height should be able to see and click the onboarding bottom actions instead of getting stuck during first-run setup.

## Evidence

- Added `WindowPlacementTests` coverage for onboarding frame clamping on a 690pt short visible frame and for preserving preferred height on tall screens.
- `git diff --check`
- Attempted: `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter WindowPlacementTests` and `swift test --package-path apps/macos --filter OnboardingViewSmokeTests`; both are blocked locally because `apps/macos` requires Swift tools 6.2.0 while this machine has Apple Swift 6.1.

target.title: feat(plugins): upgrade llm_input/llm_output hooks from fire-and-forget to modifying
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`llm_input` and `llm_output` plugin hooks are fire-and-forget (observe-only). Plugins cannot block, modify, or redact LLM calls/responses. Plugin authors need the ability to intercept LLM traffic for compliance, content filtering, prompt rewriting, and response redaction.

## Why This Change Was Made

This upgrades both hooks from fire-and-forget (void) to sequential modifying hooks. Replaces the closed #61485 with a clean implementation against current `main`.

- `llm_input` handlers can now return `{ block, blockReason, prompt, systemPrompt }` to block or modify the LLM call
- `llm_output` handlers can now return `{ assistantTexts }` to replace the model response (e.g. for redaction)
- Handlers returning `void` behave identically to before (fully backward compatible)

## User Impact

- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ block: true, blockReason: "..." }` to prevent an LLM call
- Plugins registering `llm_input` hooks can return `{ prompt, systemPrompt }` to override what's sent to the model
- Plugins registering `llm_output` hooks can return `{ assistantTexts: [...] }` to replace the response (e.g. PII redaction)
- Existing plugins that return `void` are unaffected — fully backward compatible
- `allowPromptInjection=false` strips prompt/systemPrompt overrides but preserves block/blockReason

### Mutation semantics

**llm_input:**
- `prompt` / `systemPrompt`: first-setter-wins across priority-ordered handlers
- `block` / `blockReason`: sticky-true (any handler blocks; `shouldStop` exits early)
- Subject to `allowPromptInjection` policy — prompt fields stripped when `false`
- `evolveEvent` propagates the **accumulated merged result** to lower-priority handlers and resets `imagesCount` to 0
- `systemPrompt` override applied to active model session via `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt`

**llm_output:**
- `assistantTexts`: last-setter-wins with evolved event propagation
- Later hooks see prior modifications, preventing silent overwrites of higher-priority redactions

### Security boundaries

- `PluginBlockedError` sentinel skips failover/retry classification (not a transient provider failure)
- `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook` strips `prompt`/`systemPrompt` from results when `allowPromptInjection=false`
- `historyMessages` deep-cloned via `cloneHookMessages` before passing to hooks
- `lastAssistant` deep-cloned via `structuredClone` before passing to `llm_output` hooks

### Cross-runner contract

- Embedded runner: fully consumes modifying results (block, prompt/systemPrompt override, output replacement)
- Harness helpers (`runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook`): upgraded from `void` to `Promise<Result | undefined>` so CLI, Codex app-server, and Copilot runners can consume modifying results
- Backward compatible — existing fire-and-forget callers discard the promise

### Changed files

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/plugins/hook-types.ts` | Add `PluginHookLlmInputResult`, `PluginHookLlmOutputResult` types with documented mutation semantics; add `llm_input` to prompt injection hook names; update handler map signatures |
| `src/plugins/hooks.ts` | Add `evolveEvent` to `ModifyingHookPolicy`; wire into `runModifyingHook` using accumulated result; upgrade `runLlmInput`/`runLlmOutput` from `runVoidHook` to `runModifyingHook` |
| `src/plugins/registry.ts` | Add `constrainLlmInputPromptInjectionHook`; handle `llm_input` in prompt injection guard |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts` | Add `PluginBlockedError`; await `llm_input`/`llm_output` results; apply prompt/systemPrompt overrides to active session; wire output replacement |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.ts` | Import `PluginBlockedError`; handle with `hook_block` error kind, skip failover |
| `src/agents/harness/lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts` | Upgrade `runAgentHarnessLlmInputHook`/`LlmOutputHook` to return `Promise<Result>` |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts` | 18 unit tests: block, override, priority merge, A>B>C accumulated-result evolution, backward compat, error handling |
| `src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts` | 6 e2e tests: full plugin lifecycle from `api.on()` -> loader -> registry -> runner -> result |

## Evidence

### E2E plugin lifecycle proof (6 tests)

Exercises the full path from plugin `api.on()` registration through loader, registry, hook runner, to result consumption:

1. **Block**: Plugin returns `{ block: true, blockReason: "Content policy violation" }` when prompt contains "BLOCKED" — runner returns block result
2. **Prompt rewrite**: Plugin returns `{ prompt: "[SANITIZED] " + event.prompt }` — runner returns rewritten prompt
3. **System prompt override**: Plugin returns `{ systemPrompt: "compliance prompt" }` — runner returns override
4. **Output redaction**: Plugin replaces `secret` with `[REDACTED]` in `assistantTexts` via `llm_output` — runner returns redacted output
5. **Backward compat**: Plugin returns `void` from both hooks — runner returns `undefined` (no modification)
6. **allowPromptInjection=false**: Plugin returns block + prompt + systemPrompt — constraint strips prompt/systemPrompt, preserves block

### Unit tests (18 tests)

Cover hook merger internals: merge policy, evolveEvent, imagesCount reset, error handling, empty array suppression.

### Verification commands

```
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.e2e.test.ts  # 6/6 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm-modifying.test.ts      # 18/18 pass
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/wired-hooks-llm.test.ts                # 5/5 pass (backward compat)
pnpm tsgo:core && pnpm tsgo:extensions                                          # typecheck clean
```

## ClawSweeper P1 findings addressed

All 3 findings from the [initial review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103959#issuecomment-4939779091) fixed:

1. **evolveEvent uses accumulated result** — `hooks.ts`: `evolveEvent(event, result)` not `evolveEvent(event, handlerResult)`. A>B>C priority test validates.
2. **systemPrompt applied to active session** — `attempt.ts`: `setActiveSessionSystemPrompt()` called after hook override.
3. **Harness helpers return results** — `lifecycle-hook-helpers.ts`: both return `Promise<Result | undefined>` for cross-runner consumption.

## Supersedes

Replaces #61485 (closed by maintainer as stale)

target.title: fix(sessions): sessions_search slows as transcript history grows
target.body:
Closes #105581

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users searching retained sessions would experience latency that grew with total transcript history, even when every transcript search index was already healthy. In a 400-session / 400,000-event steady-state benchmark, the complete search spent about 50 ms rescanning historical rows before doing the FTS query.

## Why This Change Was Made

The reconciliation check now starts from canonical sessions and uses the transcript `(session_id, seq)` primary key to seek directly to each session's latest event. This preserves the existing missing, dirty, and lagging-watermark behavior without grouping the complete event table; the regression test exercises all three states.

This PR also refreshes the already-stale generated Plugin SDK API hash on current `main`, required for the changed-file gate to pass. It does not change Plugin SDK source or behavior.

AI-assisted: yes. The implementation and generated metadata were inspected, tested on Node 24 Testbox, and independently reviewed before commit.

## User Impact

`sessions_search` stays responsive as transcript history grows. In the history-heavy benchmark, complete search latency fell from 49.64 ms average to 0.74 ms average (about 67x faster) with unchanged results and indexing semantics.

## Evidence

Deterministic isolated benchmark, 400 sessions x 1,000 events, 50 measured runs after warmup:

| Surface | Before avg | After avg | Before p95 | After p95 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Healthy-index reconciliation | 48.97 ms | 0.32 ms | 50.32 ms | 0.41 ms |
| Complete transcript search | 49.64 ms | 0.74 ms | 51.11 ms | 0.82 ms |

target.title: feat(openrouter): inject cache_control for closed-source qwen models
target.body:
## Summary

Extend the existing OpenRouter cache_control wrapper to cover Alibaba's closed-source qwen commercial line (`qwen3-max` / `qwen3-plus` / `qwen3-flash` and future versioned tiers), in addition to `anthropic/*` models.

## Why this is safe

Closed-source qwen models on OpenRouter are served **exclusively by Alibaba (DashScope)**, which implements Anthropic-compatible `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }` markers. Routing is therefore deterministic — the marker is guaranteed to take effect, so we can inject it unconditionally with no need for explicit `provider.only` routing.

Open-source qwen models are excluded because OpenRouter routes them across multiple upstreams (Together, DeepInfra, Fireworks, etc.), most of which do not support `cache_control`. Models with middle qualifiers like `qwen3-coder-plus` and the unversioned rolling aliases (`qwen-max`, `qwen-plus`, `qwen-turbo`, `qwen-flash`) are also excluded for now because their cache_control support is less predictable across snapshots.

## Match rule

```
/^qwen\/qwen\d+(\.\d+){0,2}-(plus|max|flash)(-preview|-\d{4}(-\d{2}-\d{2})?)?$/
```

Covers:
- `qwen/qwen3-max`, `qwen/qwen3-plus`, `qwen/qwen3-flash`
- Future minor/patch versions (`qwen3.5-max`, `qwen4-max`, ...)
- Dated snapshots (`qwen3-max-2025-09-23`, `qwen3-max-2507`)
- Preview tags (`qwen3.6-max-preview`)

Excludes (covered by tests):
- Open-source: `qwen3-235b-a22b`, `qwen3-coder`, `qwq-32b`, `qwen-2.5-72b-instruct`
- Middle qualifiers: `qwen3-coder-plus`, `qwen3-vl-max`
- Unversioned aliases: `qwen-max`, `qwen-plus`, `qwen-turbo`, `qwen-flash`
- Turbo tier: `qwen3-turbo`

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests cover the truth table (7 cases, all passing)
- [x] Existing `proxy-stream-wrappers.test.ts` still passes
- [x] Live E2E verification — see results below

## Live E2E results

Tested against real OpenRouter + Alibaba upstream with `openrouter/qwen/qwen3.6-plus`, captured via `mitmdump`:

**Request body** (after wrapper patch — confirmed in captured TLS payload):
```json
{
  "model": "qwen/qwen3.6-plus",
  "messages": [
    {
      "role": "system",
      "content": [{
        "type": "text",
        "text": "...39228 chars...",
        "cache_control": { "type": "ephemeral" }
      }]
    },
    { "role": "user", "content": "Say hi in one word" }
  ]
}
```

**Response usage** (two identical-prefix calls, ~5s apart):

| Call | prompt_tokens | cached_tokens | cache_write_tokens | cost |
|------|---------------|---------------|---------------------|------|
| 1    | 8030          | 0             | **8014** ← write    | $0.003795 |
| 2    | 8030          | **8014** ← hit | 0                  | $0.000827 |

Cache hit on second call → **78% cost reduction** on the cached prefix portion. Confirms:

1. Wrapper injects `cache_control: { type: "ephemeral" }` on the system message for closed-source qwen
2. OpenRouter passes the marker through to Alibaba upstream
3. Alibaba honors the marker, writes the cache, and serves identical-prefix requests from cache

target.title: fix(media): allow private openai compatible audio transcription endpoints
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: Audio media-understanding transcription could target self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints, but audio config did not expose the private-network request opt-in used by guarded provider HTTP.
- Why it matters: Trusted local, RFC1918, or tailnet Whisper-style endpoints need explicit private-network access without globally relaxing media request SSRF policy.
- What changed: Added audio-only request config support for `tools.media.audio.request.allowPrivateNetwork`, aligned schema/generated metadata/docs, threaded audio request overrides into provider execution, and aligned OpenAI-compatible loopback audio auth with the chat-completion local auth pattern by using the shared `custom-local` marker only for loopback OpenAI-compatible audio bases.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): Image and video media request config still reject `allowPrivateNetwork`, private-network access remains disabled by default, explicit `request.auth` still injects the configured auth header, and media/audio does not add the Ollama-specific local-auth branch.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [x] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes N/A
- Related N/A
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause (if applicable)

- Root cause: Audio media config reused the generic media request schema/type path, which rejected `allowPrivateNetwork`, while provider execution needed an audio-specific trusted request override path. The local no-auth path also needed to follow the existing chat-completion pattern: synthesize the shared `custom-local` marker for loopback OpenAI-compatible endpoints, then avoid sending provider-default auth for that marker.
- Missing detection / guardrail: Existing schema and runner tests did not cover audio-specific private-network request overrides or loopback OpenAI-compatible audio endpoints without provider auth.
- Contributing context (if known): The config docs baseline and audio field metadata are generated/aligned surfaces for this config contract.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file: `src/config/schema.test.ts`, `src/media-understanding/openai-compatible-audio.test.ts`, `src/media-understanding/runner.proxy.test.ts`, `src/media-understanding/shared.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: Audio config accepts and forwards `allowPrivateNetwork`, image/video reject it, per-model audio request config works, loopback OpenAI-compatible audio can synthesize `custom-local` when provider auth is absent, synthetic local audio auth sends no provider-default `Authorization`, explicit request auth still wins, and Ollama does not get the media/audio local-auth branch.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: These tests exercise the config contract and provider request assembly without needing a live transcription service.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): N/A
- If no new test is added, why not: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users can opt audio transcription requests into private-network endpoints with `tools.media.audio.request.allowPrivateNetwork` and per-model audio request config. Loopback OpenAI-compatible audio endpoints such as `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1` can run without provider auth, matching local OpenAI-compatible chat-completion providers. The OpenAI provider docs now show the loopback example base URL.

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation: The new network capability is an explicit audio-only opt-in for trusted private endpoints; defaults remain blocked by the SSRF guard and image/video still reject the private-network flag. Local no-auth audio is restricted to loopback OpenAI-compatible audio providers using the existing non-secret `custom-local` marker. Explicit request auth still injects the configured header when present.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: Linux 6.1.0-44-cloud-amd64 x86_64
- Runtime/container: Node v22.22.2, pnpm 10.33.0
- Model/provider: OpenAI-compatible audio transcription config path

1. Parse audio, image, and video media config shapes through the runtime zod schema.
2. Run audio provider execution with provider-level, audio-level, and per-model request overrides.
3. Run provider HTTP request assembly with synthetic local auth and explicit request auth.

### Expected

- Audio request config accepts and forwards private-network opt-in only when explicitly configured.

target.title: docs(rfd): @openclaw/call-sdk — provider-agnostic real-time call SDK
target.body:
## What

Adds an RFC + two companion design docs proposing **`@openclaw/call-sdk`** — a provider-agnostic real-time call SDK — and its binding into OpenClaw's `ChannelPlugin` model.

The three docs are intentionally split so each can be reviewed independently:

| File | What |
|---|---|
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-rfd.mdx) | RFC summary: goal, non-goals, proposed interface sketch, three hard tradeoffs. Entry point that links to the two companion docs. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-design.mdx) | Portable SDK API design: `Call`, `CallTransport`, `CallTap` and built-in tap kinds (`InferenceTap`, `RecordingTap`, `CaptionTap`, `IVRTap`, `TransformTap`, `MixerTap`, `TestTap`), `MediaFrame` v1→v2 plan, fan-out / `AbortSignal` as v1 core, lifecycle observability events, v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later scope split, worked examples, phased roadmap. |
| [`docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx`](https://github.com/visionik/clawdis/blob/rfc/call-sdk/docs/refactor/call-sdk-channel-binding.mdx) | OpenClaw-side binding: `capabilities.call`, `ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`, the load-bearing "channels never tap" guardrail (enforced at types / runtime / PR docs), authority/trust boundary between channels and tap-attaching code, two-axes / two-registries split, session-key conventions with `:call:<callId>`, `channel-call-inbound` dispatch helpers, single-connection contract, real-world capability matrix, 8-phase migration path. |

You can also browse all three in the [Files changed tab](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/73606/files).

## Why

OpenClaw handles dozens of messaging channels uniformly today. Real-time calls are not — every transport (WhatsApp calling, the in-progress Google Meet integration, Twilio voice) has its own ad-hoc wiring, no shared `Call` lifecycle, no standard way to attach STT/TTS, no recording, no captions. Every new transport reinvents the same patterns.

This RFC proposes the missing shared layer: a portable `@openclaw/call-sdk` exposing `Call` (per-call lifecycle and media surface) and `CallTap` (anything that consumes or produces media on a call), plus a thin OpenClaw binding (`ChannelPlugin.call: ChannelCallAdapter`) so a single channel package per platform can own both messaging and calls cleanly.

## Three hard tradeoffs (decided)

1. **`Buffer` v1, `MediaFrame` v2.** Ship `AsyncIterable<Buffer>` now to unblock the abstractions; design `MediaFrame` (codec / sample-rate / sequence / track / EOS / error) against real codec needs in v2.
2. **Multi-tap composition over single-bridge.** Many `CallTap`s per call, independent. Requires fan-out + `AbortSignal` cancellation to be boringly correct in v1 core, not v1.1 polish — otherwise detach leaks pipelines.
3. **Policy lives in the host, not the SDK.** `attachTap(call, tap)` is a plain function. OpenClaw wraps it as `core.attachTap(...)` under RBAC; the SDK exposes only attach/detach observability events for hosts to wire consent, audit, and recording-disclosure on top.

## Scope of this PR

**Docs only.** No code, no package added. The RFC asks for review of the design before any implementation begins; companion docs spell out the v1 / v1.1 / v2 / later split so reviewers can see the implementation-phase shape without that work being part of this PR.

## Open questions worth surfacing at RFD level

- Should `messaging` become optional on `ChannelPlugin` so call-only platforms (Meet, PSTN) are first-class? (Recommended: yes.)
- Should the plugin-sdk module path be `channel-call` (matches the renamed cap and SDK) or stay `channel-voice` (matches existing `realtime-voice` registry vocabulary)? (Recommended: `channel-call`.)

## External draft references

These docs were synthesized from in-progress drafts; gists kept until the RFD is merged for reviewers who want the change history:

- Call-SDK design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/e95177cc29fe5f9b8d7bb983635a520c
- Channel-plugin design gist: https://gist.github.com/visionik/6d27c758552403ea4b4641c72d73ebda

---

target.title: feat(exec): inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID env vars for child processes
target.body:
## Summary
Inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` environment variables into child processes spawned by the exec tool, allowing scripts and skills to reliably identify the current session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

Supersedes #68859 with full coverage including node-host execution, regression tests, and docs updates.

Closes #66705

## Problem
Currently, skills and scripts executed via exec have no reliable way to determine which session or agent they belong to. While the model can pass these identifiers as parameters, this approach is prone to hallucination errors where the model may provide incorrect values.

This blocks workflows where a child process needs to register a callback or webhook that routes back to the originating session.

## Solution
Automatically inject `OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY` and `OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID` into the environment of child processes spawned by exec, across all execution paths.

### Changes

**Core injection:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.ts` — inject both vars in `runExecProcess` (`shellRuntimeEnv`)
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.ts` — inject both vars in `shellRuntimeEnv` after sanitization for `host=node` execution
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.ts` — pass `agentId` through gateway allowlist path

**Type updates:**
- Added `agentId?: string` to `runExecProcess` opts type

**Documentation:**
- `docs/help/environment.md` — document both new env vars
- `docs/tools/exec.md` — note session/agent injection for all exec hosts

**Tests:**
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec.path.test.ts` — 6 new tests covering gateway injection, user env override prevention, and empty-string clearing semantics
- `src/node-host/invoke-system-run.test.ts` — updated sanitizer allowlist test to verify trusted var injection
- `src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts` — removed stale test (gateway no longer injects vars into `requestedEnv`)

## Testing
- [x] Local gateway execution (host=gateway)
- [x] Sandbox execution (host=sandbox) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] PTY mode (pty=true) — covered by shared shellRuntimeEnv path
- [x] Node-host execution (host=node) — unit tests in invoke-system-run.test.ts
- [x] Override semantics — user env cannot override trusted values
- [x] Clearing semantics — empty string when no agent/session defaults provided

## Usage Example
```python
import os
session_key = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY")
agent_id = os.environ.get("OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID")
```

## Backward Compatibility
Fully backward compatible:
- Variables always set (empty string when not available), avoiding stale-value issues
- Trusted values override any user-provided env overrides with the same names
- No existing behavior changed

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Inject OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID environment variables into exec child processes so skills and scripts can reliably identify their session and agent without relying on model parameter passing.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw 2026.4.2, macOS arm64, gateway mode

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
1. Built and ran OpenClaw gateway with the patched code
2. Created a minimal test skill at workspace/skills/test-env-injection/ that prints both environment variables
3. Executed the skill script via the exec tool within a main agent session
4. Captured the console output

**Evidence after fix**:
```bash
$ python3 ~/.openclaw/workspace/skills/test-env-injection/test.py
agent:main:2
main
```

**Observed result after fix**: Both OPENCLAW_SESSION_KEY and OPENCLAW_AGENT_ID are correctly injected into the exec child process environment. The output matches the expected session key (agent:main:2) and agent id (main).

**What was not tested**: Node-host (host=node) execution path was not tested in a real multi-node setup; only unit tests cover this path.

target.title: Fix/gateway silent revocation failures
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Three bare `catch {}` blocks in the gateway WebSocket revocation paths (`server-shared-auth-generation.ts:28,43` and `server-request-context.ts:116`) silently swallow `socket.close()` failures. When an admin rotates gateway auth or removes a compromised device, a failing close leaves the evicted client connected with no log and no fallback.
- **Why it matters:** On the device-removal path, this is a fail-open security gap — an admin removes a compromised device, the close throws, the attacker keeps their authenticated WebSocket connection. The operator sees no indication that revocation was partial.
- **What changed:** Replaced all three bare catches with log-then-terminate: capture the error, warn with connId/deviceId/message, fall back to `socket.terminate()`. Extracted a shared `forceCloseSharedAuthClient` helper and `describeRevocationError` utility.
- **What did NOT change:** No changes to auth logic, pairing, session management, or any non-revocation paths.

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Auth / tokens

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #70515 (same bare-catch pattern found in config recovery)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** Bare `catch {}` around `socket.close()` in three revocation loops.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No test injected a throwing `socket.close()` on the revocation path.
- **Contributing context:** The catch structure is intentional (rethrowing would kill the eviction loop for sibling clients), but the silent swallow is not.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level: [x] Unit test
- **Scenario:** Inject a throwing `socket.close`, assert (a) `logger.warn` fires with connId + error message, (b) `terminate()` is called as fallback, (c) remaining clients in the iterable still get evicted.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Operators now see a warning log when a revocation close fails. Failed closes fall back to `socket.terminate()` — the evicted client is now force-killed even when the graceful close throws.

## Diagram

```text
Before:
[socket.close() throws] -> [catch {}] -> [attacker keeps connection] -> [no log]

After:
[socket.close() throws] -> [warn log with connId + error] -> [socket.terminate()] -> [connection killed]
```

## Security Impact

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** Bare `catch {}` blocks around `socket.close()` in the three gateway WebSocket revocation paths silently swallowed failures. When a device removal or shared-auth rotation triggered a close that threw, the evicted client stayed connected with no log and no fallback — a fail-open security gap on the device-removal path.

**Real environment tested:** macOS 25.4.0 / Node 23.7.0, project source checkout, `node --import tsx/esm` run directly against the call-chain pattern.

**Exact steps or command run after the patch:**
```
node --import tsx/esm proof-70676.mts
```

**Evidence after fix:**

Before the fix (bare `catch {}`):
```
=== BEFORE FIX (bare catch {}) ===
  Warned: none (silent failure)
  Terminated as fallback: none — conn-bad may still be connected!
```

After the fix (warn + terminate fallback):
```
=== AFTER FIX (warn + terminate fallback) ===
  Warned: "revocation close failed for connId=conn-bad: Error: socket already destroyed — attempting terminate()"
  Terminated as fallback: conn-bad ✓ — attacker connection killed
  conn-healthy untouched: yes ✓
```

**Observed result after fix:** Failed revocation closes now log a warning with the `connId` and error message, fall back to `socket.terminate()` to force-kill the connection, and continue evicting remaining clients in the loop. The fail-open gap is closed.

**What was not tested:** Full integration test with real WebSocket in half-closed state. The `node` script above isolates the exact three-branch pattern and produces real before/after terminal output demonstrating the silent failure and its fix.

target.title: fix(auto-reply): dedupe idless inbound retries
target.body:
## Summary
- add a content/timestamp fallback inbound dedupe key when providers do not supply a stable message id
- keep normal provider-message-id dedupe unchanged
- cover idless retry dedupe and same-body/different-timestamp non-collapse

## Why
Some channel retry paths can re-enter auto-reply without a stable provider message id. In that case the current inbound dedupe returns invalid and the retry can be injected again. The fallback is scoped by provider/account/session/peer/thread plus a 128-bit SHA-256 prefix over timestamp and body, so ordinary provider-id paths keep their existing behavior while idless retries get a deterministic backstop.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: idless inbound retries should be suppressed when they carry the same route, timestamp, and text body, while distinct same-body messages and attachment-only idless messages should not be collapsed.

Real environment tested: rebased patched OpenClaw source checkout at `/tmp/openclaw-72314`, Node 24, directly invoking the real `src/auto-reply/reply/inbound-dedupe.ts` module through `tsx`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-72314-proof.mjs
```

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where WhatsApp channel payloads containing both `mediaUrls` and the legacy `mediaUrl` field sent the legacy attachment first. Channel payloads are expected to prefer a usable plural list and use the single URL only as a fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

The WhatsApp channel `sendPayload` boundary now normalizes plural media entries first, then passes the payload through `resolvePayloadMediaUrls` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/reply-payload`. This makes a non-empty, usable `mediaUrls` list authoritative while preserving `mediaUrl` fallback for omitted, empty, or whitespace-only plural lists. Tests update the channel expectation and cover plural precedence, legacy fallback, empty arrays, whitespace-only arrays, trimming, deduplication, and the preserved direct-API behavior.

WhatsApp channel replies now send the attachments selected by the canonical channel payload contract. Existing direct callers of `sendMessageWhatsApp` retain their previous media selection behavior.

target.title: fix(line): skip confirm/buttons templates with blank required fields
target.body:
Fixes #105511

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a LINE reply is silently dropped when the agent uses a `[[confirm:]]` or `[[buttons:]]` directive with a blank required field. The user gets nothing back — not just the confirm dialog or button card, but any text sent in the same turn. It's easy to hit because an LLM will occasionally leave one of the pipe-separated fields empty.

## Why This Change Was Made

Both directives only checked that the fields were present (`parts.length >= 3`), not that the required ones were non-empty. A blank field produced a template with an empty required property, which LINE rejects with HTTP 400, so the whole payload — directive and surrounding text — is dropped. The fix skips building the template when a required field is blank: the directive markup is still stripped and the rest of the reply sends, so a malformed directive degrades to plain text instead of losing the message.

Same failure family as #105381 (empty Flex text), on the template fields rather than the comma lists. The flex-card directives (`[[event:]]`, `[[media_player:]]`, `[[device:]]`, `[[appletv_remote:]]`) already avoid it with `title || "fallback"`, and the `/card` command uses literal defaults, so only these two directives were missing the guard.

## User Impact

When the agent emits a slightly malformed confirm/buttons directive, LINE users now receive the rest of the reply as plain text instead of silence. Any message text sent alongside the directive is no longer collateral of the 400. No change for well-formed directives.

## Evidence

Each blank field, run through the parser and posted to LINE's `validate/push` endpoint (validates the payload without sending). Before, on `origin/main`:

```
[[confirm:  | Yes | No]]         -> 400 "May not be empty"        @ messages[0].altText
[[confirm: Q |  | No]]           -> 400 "must be non-empty text"  @ template/actions/0/label
[[confirm: Q | Yes | ]]          -> 400 "must be non-empty text"  @ template/actions/1/label
[[buttons:  | Choose | Opt1:d1]] -> 400 "must be non-empty text"  @ template/title
[[buttons: Menu |  | Opt1:d1]]   -> 400 "must be non-empty text"  @ template/text
```

After the fix, all of these skip the template — nothing invalid is sent — including whitespace-only and all-blank variants. A valid directive still builds and validates 200. And a directive mixed with text keeps the text: `"Please decide: [[confirm:  | Yes | No]]"` sends `"Please decide:"` instead of dropping the whole reply.

New tests cover the five blank cases, the surrounding-text preservation, and the valid controls. Red on `main`, green with the fix:

```
without fix: Tests  3 failed | 13 passed (16)
  x skips confirm when the question or a label is blank
  x skips buttons when the title or text is blank
  x keeps the rest of the reply when a blank directive is skipped
with fix:    Tests  16 passed (16)
```

Full `extensions/line` suite green, extensions typecheck clean.

target.title: feat: PluginStatusProvider plugin API for TUI footer status (resolves #64086)
target.body:
Resolves #64086. Coordinates with #53774 (broader footer-customization tracker).

## What this PR does

Adds a typed `PluginStatusProvider` interface and `registerStatusProvider` method to `OpenClawPluginApi`, following the same registration shape as `registerTool` / `registerHook`. Providers are stored in the plugin registry under a new `statusProviders` field.

```ts
export type PluginStatusProvider = {
  /** A unique identifier for this provider. */
  id: string;
  /** Function returning the status string, or null/undefined to hide it. */
  getStatus: () => string | null | undefined;
};
```

Plugin author usage:

```ts
api.registerStatusProvider({
  id: "contextclaw.savings",
  getStatus: () => `cc: -${savedPercent}%`,
});
```

## Scope

This PR lands the API/registry seam only:

- `PluginStatusProvider` type and `registerStatusProvider` API entry on `OpenClawPluginApi`.
- Plugin registry storage under `statusProviders`.
- API builder and plugin-entry SDK exposure.
- Duplicate, blank, and normalized-id validation.
- Loader rollback coverage so a provider registered by a plugin that later fails registration is removed with the rest of that plugin's side effects.

Explicitly not included:

- TUI render-path wire-up. That should stay in a follow-up once maintainers accept the API shape, ordering, truncation, theming, and footer placement.
- Cost-display footer changes. Those were split out of #64127 and can be revisited under #53774.

## Plugin-author motivation

I'm shipping [ContextClaw](https://github.com/dodge1218/contextclaw), a context-engine plugin that currently has to monkeypatch the bundled TUI to surface live stats. That breaks on OpenClaw release churn. A first-class `registerStatusProvider` seam gives plugins a supported path.

## Real behavior proof

Behavior or issue addressed: A native plugin can call `api.registerStatusProvider(...)` during OpenClaw plugin registration, OpenClaw stores the provider in the plugin registry, and failed plugin registration rolls back status-provider side effects instead of leaving stale status entries.

Real environment tested:
- Current PR head: `1ff80b48b86c8bc6b6f34fd03cf2bf84a2f9bce0`.
- OpenClaw plugin loader/registry path from this branch.
- Earlier full dogfood proof used the real ContextClaw plugin and a real local OpenClaw gateway. The current-head follow-up below specifically covers the review blockers added after that proof: rollback, SDK baseline, and release-owned changelog scope.

Exact steps or command run after the patch:

```bash
pnpm plugin-sdk:api:check

OPENCLAW_VITEST_NO_OUTPUT_TIMEOUT_MS=120000 timeout 240s \
  pnpm exec node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run \
  --config test/vitest/vitest.plugins.config.ts \
  src/plugins/registry.status-provider.test.ts \
  src/plugins/loader.test.ts \
  -t 'status provider|rolls back status providers'

pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 \
  src/plugins/loader.ts \
  src/plugins/loader.test.ts \
  src/plugins/registry.ts \
  src/plugins/registry.status-provider.test.ts \
  src/plugins/api-builder.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry.ts \
  docs/plugins/sdk-overview.md \
  docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256 \
  CHANGELOG.md

git diff --check
```

Evidence after fix:

```text
plugin-sdk:api:check: OK docs/.generated/plugin-sdk-api-baseline.sha256
focused Vitest status-provider/rollback tests: exit 0
oxfmt: All matched files use the correct format.
git diff --check: exit 0
```

Observed result after fix:

- Duplicate and blank status-provider ids are rejected with diagnostics.
- Padded status-provider ids are normalized before storage and duplicate comparison.
- A plugin that registers a status provider and then throws during registration leaves `registry.statusProviders` empty after loader rollback.
- The public Plugin SDK API baseline hash is regenerated for the new `PluginStatusProvider` export.
- The direct `CHANGELOG.md` edit was removed; release-note context stays in the PR body.

Earlier real runtime proof, preserved for the plugin-author path:

```text

```

What was not tested: TUI footer rendering, ordering, truncation, and theming. This PR intentionally lands only the plugin API/registry seam.

## Coordination with #53774

#53774 is the broader tracker for custom footer fields such as cost, balance, rate-limit status, and footer templates. This PR is the plugin-API piece of that direction. It does not preempt the footer-template decisions.

## Open questions for reviewers

- Naming: `getStatus` vs `render` vs `getText`.
- Return shape: `string | null | undefined` now, or `{ text, color }` upfront.
- Multiple providers per plugin: the registry allows it; happy to restrict or document it.

target.title: fix(signal): await daemon shutdown on restart
target.body:
## Summary
- make Signal daemon shutdown asynchronous and await process exit
- fall back to SIGKILL if signal-cli does not exit after SIGTERM
- add regression coverage for daemon stop semantics and aborted monitor shutdown

## Testing
- corepack pnpm exec vitest run extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.autostart.test.ts
- corepack pnpm exec vitest run extensions/signal/src

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: Signal auto-start monitor shutdown/restart must wait for the spawned daemon process to exit instead of returning while the daemon is still alive, preventing orphaned `signal-cli daemon` processes across abort/restart paths.
- Real environment tested: macOS 14.8.5 arm64 on a local OpenClaw checkout, Node v22.22.2, PR head `3fa74e98e72de378366b4dc5d48cae5f6dd21249`. The machine does not have a linked Signal account or `signal-cli` installed, so this proof used the real OpenClaw Signal monitor/daemon lifecycle code with a local signal-cli-compatible child process that exposes `/api/v1/check` and `/api/v1/events`; no external Signal messages were sent.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
cd /Users/zhoukailian/Desktop/mySelf/openclaw/.worktrees/fix-signal-daemon-stop-race
node --import tsx /tmp/openclaw-signal-lifecycle-proof.mjs | tee /tmp/openclaw-signal-lifecycle-proof.out
```

- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "repoHead": "3fa74e98e72de378366b4dc5d48cae5f6dd21249",
  "baseMain": "e0225380a7454a85db1038e495d18a28b5d918ed",
  "port": 20031,
  "pid": 34488,
  "aliveBeforeAbort": true,
  "monitorResolved": true,
  "resolveWaitMs": 659,
  "aliveAfterMonitorResolved": false,
  "elapsedMs": 867,
  "events": "START pid=34488 args=[\"daemon\",\"--http\",\"127.0.0.1:20031\",\"--no-receive-stdout\",\"--receive-mode\",\"manual\"]\nSIGTERM pid=34488 at=1778304230573\nEXIT_AFTER_SIGTERM pid=34488 at=1778304231225",
  "runtimeLogs": [
    {
      "level": "log",
      "t": 200,
      "msg": "signal-cli: signal-cli shim READY pid=34488 http=127.0.0.1:20031"
    },
    {
      "level": "error",
      "t": 867,
      "msg": "signal daemon exited (source=process code=0 signal=null)"
    }
  ]
}
```

- Observed result after fix: The Signal monitor started the daemon child process, verified it was alive before abort, sent SIGTERM on abort, waited about 659ms for the child to finish its shutdown, then resolved only after the process exited. `aliveAfterMonitorResolved: false` confirms there was no leftover daemon process after `monitorSignalProvider` returned.
- What was not tested: A live linked Signal account, real `signal-cli` network traffic, actual inbound/outbound Signal message delivery, or the macOS LaunchAgent restart path. This proof is scoped to the changed OpenClaw daemon lifecycle behavior and avoids sending external Signal messages from the test machine.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): The regression tests added in this PR demonstrate the previous behavior: on unpatched main, `stop()` returned `undefined` instead of a promise and there was no SIGKILL escalation. The live proof above verifies the patched after-fix runtime behavior on this machine.

## Root Cause

- Root cause: Signal daemon shutdown was fire-and-forget. `stop()` only sent SIGTERM and returned immediately, so monitor abort/restart could continue while the old daemon process was still shutting down.
- Missing detection / guardrail: There was no regression coverage asserting that daemon stop returns a promise, waits for process exit, is idempotent across overlapping callers, and escalates to SIGKILL when SIGTERM does not finish.
- Contributing context (if known): `signal-cli` daemon shutdown can be slow enough that immediate restart paths race with the previous process still owning resources.

## Regression Test Plan

- Coverage level that should have caught this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target test or file:
  - `extensions/signal/src/daemon.test.ts`
  - `extensions/signal/src/monitor.tool-result.autostart.test.ts`
- Scenario the test should lock in: `stop()` waits for daemon exit after SIGTERM, escalates to SIGKILL after the timeout, reuses an in-flight stop promise, and `monitorSignalProvider` awaits daemon stop before resolving aborted shutdown.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: It exercises the Signal daemon lifecycle seam directly without requiring a live Signal account or sending external messages.
- Existing test that already covers this (if any): None before this PR.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Signal auto-start restart/shutdown should leave fewer orphaned daemon processes. Shutdown may now wait briefly for `signal-cli daemon` to exit; if it does not exit after SIGTERM, OpenClaw escalates to SIGKILL after the configured timeout.

Closes #22676

target.title: media: add shared filename decoder
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: filename decoding is split across media/channel paths, so `Content-Disposition` edge cases and Feishu mojibake fixes are easy to miss or duplicate.
- Why it matters: attachment names with RFC 5987 language tags, non-UTF-8 charset labels, Windows path separators, or UTF-8 bytes misread as Latin-1/Windows-1252 can be saved or delivered with confusing names.
- What changed: added shared media filename decoding helpers, wired remote media fetch through them, and exposed Feishu filename mojibake recovery through the Feishu plugin SDK surface for inbound saves.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): this does not migrate every channel filename path yet, so it is a partial implementation of the broader centralized utility work.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #48788
- Related #48388

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Remote media downloads now preserve more `Content-Disposition` filenames correctly, including RFC 5987 language-tagged values and explicit GB18030, Shift_JIS, and EUC-KR charset labels. Feishu inbound filenames that arrive as UTF-8 mojibake are recovered before saving when possible.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS / local Codex worktree
- Runtime/container: Node 22.16.0 via corepack pnpm
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): media fetch, Feishu filename handling
- Relevant config (redacted): N/A

### Steps

1. Parse RFC 5987 `Content-Disposition` filenames with language tags and explicit charset labels.
2. Fetch remote media with quoted Windows-style header filenames.
3. Recover Feishu-style UTF-8 bytes interpreted as Latin-1/Windows-1252 before saving inbound filenames.

### Expected

- Filename decoding returns readable basenames for supported encoded values.
- Remote media fetch uses the shared decoder.
- Feishu inbound mojibake recovery happens before `saveMediaBuffer` receives the filename.

### Actual

Matches expected in targeted tests.

## Evidence

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

Targeted verification:

```shell
corepack pnpm exec vitest run --config vitest.unit.config.ts src/media/filename.test.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts
corepack pnpm exec oxfmt --check src/media/filename.ts src/media/filename.test.ts src/media/fetch.ts src/media/fetch.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/feishu.ts extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts
```

`corepack pnpm tsgo` was also run. It still fails on pre-existing repo/toolchain errors unrelated to this change, including missing exports from `@mariozechner/pi-ai` and existing call-signature errors; after fixing one local Feishu compile error, no remaining tsgo error pointed at the touched files.

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: RFC 5987 `filename*` priority, language tags, GB18030 / Shift_JIS / EUC-KR decoding, Windows path basename reduction, Latin-1/Windows-1252 mojibake recovery, remote media fetch integration.
- Edge cases checked: quoted semicolons in filenames, control character stripping, `.`/`..` rejection, normal Latin-1 text fallback.
- What you did **not** verify: live Feishu file receipt against the Feishu API; full migration of Telegram/Discord/Slack filename paths.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes
- Config/env changes? No
- Migration needed? No

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: revert this PR.
- Files/config to restore: `src/media/filename.ts`, `src/media/fetch.ts`, `src/plugin-sdk/feishu.ts`, `extensions/feishu/src/bot.ts`, and related tests.
- Known bad symptoms reviewers should watch for: unexpected filename recovery for unusual Latin-1-only filenames, or plugin SDK export bundling issues.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: heuristic mojibake recovery could rewrite a valid Latin-1 filename.
  - Mitigation: recovery only applies when the decoded result is valid UTF-8 and contains non-Latin script characters; normal Latin-1 text is covered by tests.
- Risk: not all channel paths use the new utility yet.
  - Mitigation: PR is scoped as a partial implementation and links #48788 for follow-up migration.


## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: Remote media filename decoding now handles RFC 5987 language-tagged filenames, mojibake plain filenames, and Windows-style path basenames before exposing/saving the filename.
- Real environment tested: macOS local OpenClaw worktree, Node v22.16.0 via corepack pnpm, PR branch rebased onto openclaw/main 5955f354f7.
