
Harness shape: production `uploadAndShareSharePoint()` / `uploadToSharePoint()` helpers, real Node HTTP loopback server, real `fetch()` transport to loopback, redacted token provider, and a transport shim that redirects Microsoft Graph/SharePoint URLs to loopback paths. This is intentionally not described as a live Microsoft tenant run.

target.title: fix(embeddings): bound openai-compatible requests without AbortSignal
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP calls only forwarded an optional caller `AbortSignal`. Gateway `/v1/embeddings` and capability-CLI paths call `embed` / `embedBatch` without a signal, so a server that accepts the TCP connection but never sends headers could hang the request forever. Memory/wiki callers already install their own deadlines; this gap is the unsignaled transport path.

## Why This Change Was Made

When `signal` is omitted, install operation-specific hang bounds via existing `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs`:

- `embed` (query): 60s — aligned with memory remote query defaults
- `embedBatch` (batch): 120s — aligned with memory remote batch defaults so gateway/CLI batches are not clamped below established batch policy

When a caller already provides a signal, leave that deadline alone so memory search / tool timeouts are not clamped.

No new config surface. Test-only override shortens the floor for hang repros.

## User Impact

**Before:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding requests (gateway HTTP embeddings, capability CLI) could hang indefinitely on a stalled upstream.

**After:** Unsignaled query requests fail after 60s; unsignaled batch requests fail after 120s (`TimeoutError` / `request timed out`). Callers that pass `AbortSignal` keep their own budget.

## Evidence

- Changed: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.ts` (`postEmbeddingRequest`, query/batch floors)
- Production caller under test: `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider(...).provider.embed` / `embedBatch` against a real local `node:http` server that never responds
- Regression: `src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts`
- Sibling cases still green in the same file (UTF-16 error bounds, oversized JSON cancel, auth/config paths)

### Unit regression

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

```text
 ✓ |plugins| ... > uses distinct no-signal floors for query and batch 0ms
 ✓ |plugins| ... > times out embedding requests that never respond when caller omits signal 61ms
 ✓ |plugins| ... > times out unsignaled batch requests that never respond 53ms
 ✓ |plugins| ... > keeps query and batch no-signal floors independent 307ms
 ✓ |plugins| ... > keeps caller AbortSignal deadlines instead of the no-signal transport floor 205ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 27.79s
```

### Standalone runtime proof (outside Vitest)

```bash
node --import tsx <<'EOF'
# production createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider().provider.embedBatch / embed
# against real hung node:http (accepts body, never writes response)
EOF
```

```text
standalone-proof: openai-compatible embedding no-signal hang bounds
{"queryDefaultMs":60000,"batchDefaultMs":120000}
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 180ms (elapsed 181ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:49522/v1/embeddings
{"proof":"standalone-production-provider-embedBatch-no-signal","path":"createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider().provider.embedBatch","callerShape":"gateway embeddings-http / capability CLI (unsignaled)","upstream":"real node:http accepts body, never writes response","batchResult":{"ok":false,"error":{"name":"TimeoutError","message":"request timed out"}},"batchElapsedMs":207,"expectedFloorMs":180,"rejectedBeforeHangCap":true}
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 80ms (elapsed 80ms) operation=fetchWithSsrFGuard url=http://127.0.0.1:49522/v1/embeddings
{"proof":"standalone-production-provider-embed-no-signal","path":"createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider().provider.embed","queryResult":{"ok":false,"error":{"name":"TimeoutError","message":"request timed out"}},"queryElapsedMs":85,"expectedFloorMs":80,"rejectedBeforeHangCap":true}
{"proof":"standalone-caller-AbortSignal-not-clamped","signaled":{"type":"still-pending"}}
standalone-proof: done
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Unsignaled openai-compatible embedding POSTs no longer hang forever when the upstream accepts the connection but never responds; query and batch use distinct floors (60s / 120s).
- **Canonical reachability path:** gateway `embeddings-http` / capability CLI / direct provider → `createOpenAICompatibleEmbeddingProvider` → `embed` (query) or `embedBatch` (batch) → `postEmbeddingRequest` → `fetchWithSsrFGuard({ timeoutMs })` when `signal` is absent.
- **Boundary crossed:** Operator/remote OpenAI-compatible embedding HTTP → local AbortSignal timeout via guarded fetch.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reuses `fetchWithSsrFGuard` `timeoutMs` / `buildTimeoutAbortSignal`. Query/batch floors match memory-core remote budgets (`60_000` / `120_000`). Does not override caller-owned signals used by memory-core `runEmbeddingOperationWithTimeout`. Does not add config/env.
- **Real environment tested:** Local Node 22 source checkout on macOS; production provider path via standalone `node --import tsx` (outside Vitest) against real `http.createServer` on `127.0.0.1` that reads the body and never writes a response; shortened test floors for hang repro.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/plugins/openai-compatible-embedding-provider.test.ts --reporter=verbose
node --import tsx  # standalone production provider embedBatch/embed against hung socket
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
Unit:
 ✓ ... > uses distinct no-signal floors for query and batch
 ✓ ... > times out embedding requests that never respond when caller omits signal 61ms
 ✓ ... > times out unsignaled batch requests that never respond 53ms
 ✓ ... > keeps query and batch no-signal floors independent 307ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  34 passed (34)

Standalone (outside Vitest):
{"queryDefaultMs":60000,"batchDefaultMs":120000}
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 180ms ... embedBatch → TimeoutError
[fetch-timeout] fetch timeout after 80ms ... embed → TimeoutError
{"proof":"standalone-caller-AbortSignal-not-clamped","signaled":{"type":"still-pending"}}
standalone-proof: done
```

- **Observed result after fix:** Unsignaled `embedBatch` (gateway/CLI shape) and `embed` reject with `TimeoutError` / `request timed out` on a real hung socket; defaults are 60s query / 120s batch; caller-provided `AbortSignal` is not clamped by the no-signal floor.
- **What was not tested:** Live public embedding APIs; full gateway HTTP `/v1/embeddings` end-to-end against a hung upstream; memory-core batch paths (already signal-backed).
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

- [x] AI-assisted (Cursor)
- [x] I understand what the code does
- [x] Change is focused and does not mix unrelated concerns

target.title: fix(tools): bound release metadata reads when installing helpers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where helper tool installation could buffer an oversized GitHub release metadata response through the convenience JSON reader when checking the latest fd/rg release before downloading a helper binary.

## Why This Change Was Made

The helper installer now reads release metadata through the existing bounded HTTP body reader before parsing the same JSON payload. This keeps the change inside the agent tool installer boundary, preserves the guarded fetch release cleanup, and does not change helper selection, download policy, config, provider behavior, or valid release metadata handling.

## User Impact

Users and operators get the same helper auto-install behavior for normal GitHub release metadata, while unexpectedly large metadata responses are rejected at the bounded read boundary instead of being fully buffered.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: helper release metadata checks use the bounded response reader for real GitHub release metadata and do not call `response.json()` while parsing successful metadata.
- Commands / artifacts:
  - Current-head proof at `ab12af1382608646aae2e8f47d5d61663b195e1f`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` imported `fetchWithSsrFGuard` and `readResponseWithLimit`, used `auditContext: "tools-manager-release-check"`, and fetched `https://api.github.com/repos/BurntSushi/ripgrep/releases/latest`.
  - Runtime output: `status: 200`, `ok: true`, `bytes: 50552`, `maxBytes: 1048576`, `tag_name: "15.1.0"`, `parsedVersion: "15.1.0"`, `responseJsonCalled: false`.
  - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/utils/tools-manager.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 9 tests passing.
  - `git diff --check` passed.
- Observed result: the same guarded fetch plus bounded-reader sequence used by `tools-manager.ts` successfully parsed a real ripgrep helper release metadata response below the 1 MiB cap, and the focused regression still verifies an oversized 1 MiB + 1 byte metadata response is rejected without using the convenience JSON reader.

target.title: fix(active-memory): bound timeout circuit breakers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Active Memory's process-local `timeoutCircuitBreaker` map could grow without bound: entries were only removed when the same key was checked after cooldown or after a later success, so distinct failing agent/provider/model combinations that were never revisited stayed for the process lifetime.

## Why This Change Was Made

Bound the map on its owner mutation path (`recordCircuitBreakerTimeout`): purge cooldown-expired entries using the normalized configured `circuitBreakerCooldownMs`, then evict oldest `lastTimeoutAt` until under `DEFAULT_MAX_CACHE_ENTRIES` (1000) before inserting a new key. Updating an existing key refreshes counters/time and purges expired peers without evicting the active key.

## User Impact

**Before:** Each new failing agent/provider/model pair could permanently add process state; purge ignored non-default cooldowns.
**After:** Peer purge honors configured cooldown (5s–600s); remaining breaker state has a hard cap of 1000 keys.

## Evidence

- Base: `4289c6c16cd5` / Head: `e5f35dad40`
- Node: v24.18.0 / Windows
- Production Map proof (`node --import tsx` on `recordCircuitBreakerTimeout`): insert 1005 → size 1000, oldest evicted, newest kept
- Focused vitest for cooldown purge + bound + runtime hook path green
- CI: `check-test-types` fixed for the runtime-proof test

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Live gateway Active Memory recall timeouts record distinct agent keys; a follow-up turn within cooldown skips recall with `circuit breaker open`.
**Environment tested:** Windows, Node v24.18.0, worktree `codex/active-memory-bound-timeout-breakers`, real gateway child process with `plugins.slots.memory=memory-core` and `plugins.entries.active-memory` enabled; webchat Control UI client; hang recall provider (TCP accept, no HTTP response); fail-fast main provider (HTTP 401).
**Steps run after the patch:**
1. Start ephemeral gateway with agents `am0`/`am1`/`am2`, `timeoutMs=800`, `circuitBreakerMaxTimeouts=1`, `circuitBreakerCooldownMs=600000`, `logging=true`.
2. Send webchat `chat.send` for each agent (distinct timeout keys).
3. Immediately re-send for `am0` within cooldown.
**Evidence after fix:**

```text
[plugins] active-memory: agent=am0 session=<redacted> activeProvider=hang activeModel=slow done status=timeout elapsedMs=2566 summaryChars=0
[plugins] active-memory: agent=am1 session=<redacted> activeProvider=hang activeModel=slow done status=timeout elapsedMs=4855 summaryChars=0
[plugins] active-memory: agent=am2 session=<redacted> activeProvider=hang activeModel=slow done status=timeout elapsedMs=4844 summaryChars=0
[plugins] active-memory: agent=am0 session=<redacted> activeProvider=hang activeModel=slow skipped (circuit breaker open after consecutive timeouts)
```

Also observed gateway ready line listing both `active-memory` and `memory-core` among loaded plugins.
**Observed result:** `timeoutLogCount=3`, `breakerSkipLogCount=1` on the live gateway path.
**Not tested:** 1000-key cap soak under multi-hour live gateway load (covered by production Map unit/production-function proof).

target.title: fix(web): apply Control UI text size to content typography
target.body:
## Summary

In this PR, the Appearance text-size setting applies across Control UI content typography instead of only affecting the chat transcript. Shared content font sizes now route through `--control-ui-text-scale`, while touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing 16px minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not reintroduce mobile Safari focus zoom.

## Screenshots

Settings at the default M text size, showing the Appearance text-size control in English.

![Settings text size at M](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-settings-text-size-m-en.png)

Overview at XXL text size, showing the larger page typography across cards and form controls.

![Overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-overview-xxl-en.png)

Channels at XXL text size, showing the larger channel cards and actions.

![Channels using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-channels-xxl-en.png)

Mobile Overview at XXL text size, showing the narrow layout with scaled content typography.

![Mobile overview using XXL text size](https://mystic-bonnet-p3d4.here.now/pr-100934-mobile-overview-xxl-en.png)

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes the Appearance text-size setting so it affects Control UI content typography beyond the chat transcript. Before this PR, the setting could be saved while many Settings, quick settings, overview, channel, session, skill, and content surfaces still used fixed font sizes.

## Why This Change Was Made

In this PR, shared Control UI font sizes route through the existing `--control-ui-text-scale` value instead of hard-coded pixel sizes. The change keeps layout chrome and spacing stable while letting readable content, forms, cards, chat text, composer text, and page typography respond to S/M/L/XL/XXL.

Touch-primary text-entry controls keep the existing `--control-ui-input-text-size` minimum so the 90% text-size stop does not shrink mobile inputs below 16px and reintroduce Safari focus zoom.

## User Impact

Changing Text size in Appearance now produces visible typography changes across the main product surfaces, while M remains the normal/default size.

## Validation

- `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check $(git diff --name-only --diff-filter=ACMRTUXB | tr '\n' ' ')`

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:


Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.


## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'

Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
```

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's agent-testing guidance hardcoded Blacksmith Testbox for ordinary trusted validation. That caused agents to override an existing explicit Crabbox choice such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`, even though the wrapper already supports that environment override before the repository's Blacksmith default.

## Why This Change Was Made

The testing and Crabbox skills now tell trusted agent workflows to omit `--provider` unless a specific proof or safety route requires one. This preserves the existing wrapper contract:

1. an explicitly requested/command-line provider;
2. `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`;
3. the repository `.crabbox.yaml` default (`blacksmith-testbox`).

The skills also distinguish a Crabbox-managed `local-container` run from direct host testing and require provider attribution from wrapper/config output instead of inferring AWS from the shared `cbx_...` lease prefix.

ClawSweeper correctly identified that `crabbox config show --json` does not create a user-config preference above repository config. The PR was narrowed accordingly: it no longer changes `scripts/crabbox-wrapper.mjs`, adds no merged-config precedence contract, and adds no new fail-closed startup behavior.

AI-assisted: this change was agent-tested with Claude through `acpx`, reviewed with Codex autoreview, and revised in response to ClawSweeper.

## User Impact

Developers who explicitly set `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` can run ordinary trusted agent validation on that backend without agents forcing Blacksmith Testbox. Developers without an explicit override continue to use the repository's Blacksmith Testbox default.

A configured local container still executes tests inside a Crabbox-managed Docker lease; it does not silently downgrade to host-local execution. Remote, cross-platform, untrusted-source, and Testbox-specific proof requirements continue to select their required backend explicitly.

## Evidence

- Blind `acpx claude` validation independently resolved the inherited `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container`; the prompt did not name the expected provider.
- The first agent attempt exposed a guidance defect by running the focused test directly on the host. That result was rejected, and the skills were clarified to require wrapper-managed Docker execution for `local-container`.
- Post-fix Claude runs correctly provisioned local-container Docker leases, ran the focused wrapper suite inside the containers, and cleaned up their leases.
- Final post-rebase proof:
  - base: `upstream/main` at `161525d43c4c0157a8fd4feceb2bf96cb4db5900`;

  - result: 1 test file passed; 192/192 tests passed.
- Final diff relative to `upstream/main`: two skill files only; zero wrapper/test code diff.
- `git diff --check` — passed.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:


## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. **Observed result after fix**: (a) The freshly written nested file `memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md` (two levels deep under `memory/`) was indexed by `openclaw memory index` and returned as the top match (score `0.812`) for the unique token. target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
